title: Cognitive Architecture: Designing for How We Respond to the Built Environment

findings.antecedent: Buildings creating room-like conditions / continuous lines / well-defined edges (e.g., Piazza del Campo, Rue de Rivoli, Hanover Street)
findings.consequent: People feel more at ease, gravitate to sides, move forward effortlessly, feel safer, experience less anxiety, construct mental maps, linger longer, find places walkable and engaging

findings.antecedent: Open spaces / ill-defined edge conditions (e.g., Boston City Hall Plaza, Columbia, MD curvilinear roads)
findings.consequent: People avoid centers, shun open spaces, feel less safe, experience confusion, increased alertness and psychological arousal, find places less walkable, feel lost, places become 'no man's land'

findings.antecedent: Human brain's visual processing
findings.consequent: Prioritization of faces and face-like patterns, rapid recognition of faces, emotional engagement with face-like objects, formation of emotional attachments and memories of places

findings.antecedent: Symmetrical faces and objects / symmetrical decorations
findings.consequent: Perceived as more attractive, healthier, fitter, more resilient; faster mental processing, activation of smiling muscles, feelings of calm/reassurance, aesthetic preference

findings.antecedent: Curvilinear shapes in architecture and objects
findings.consequent: Elicit feelings of happiness and elation, judged as more beautiful, preferred over rectilinear forms, reduced patient anxiety

findings.antecedent: Repetitive parallel lines / sharp-angled objects (common in modern built environments)
findings.consequent: Stress the brain, require more oxygen uptake, elicit feelings of pain and sadness, increased sense of threat and danger, amygdala activation, higher patient anxiety

findings.antecedent: Organized complexity in built environments
findings.consequent: Promotes survival, helps body maintain homeostasis/equilibrium, provides meaningful ordering, helps interpret the world and navigate, preferred over disorganized/blank arrangements

findings.antecedent: Fractal patterns (not too dense, not too sparse)
findings.consequent: Induce relaxation, generate maximal alpha response in frontal region, preferred by humans

findings.antecedent: Narrative quality / spatial sequencing in building plans or garden designs
findings.consequent: Increases ability to connect to environment, provides sense of meaning, identity, pride of place, positive town identity, uplifting story, magnifies sense of arrival

findings.antecedent: Exposure to nature / natural scenes / biophilic elements (e.g., plants, water, sunlight, tree plantings, nature murals, views of trees)
findings.consequent: Reduces stress, improves mental/physical/spiritual health, increases well-being, makes patients less nervous, shorter hospital stays, less pain medicine, increased happiness, improved child health/development, increased worker productivity, enhanced cognitive abilities, improved attendance/academic achievement, community cohesion, reduced recidivism in prisons

findings.antecedent: Lack of connection to nature / visual impoverishment (e.g., concrete canyons)
findings.consequent: Sensory deprivation, monotony, artificiality, dulling of human senses, placelessness, ADHD in children

findings.antecedent: Biometric tools (eye tracking, facial expression analysis, EEG, GSR/EDA)
findings.consequent: Reveal hidden evolutionary traits, make invisible behaviors visible, understand unconscious eye movements, decode facial expressions, measure brain waves, track emotional arousal, predict user behavior, assess walkability, evaluate imageability, inform evidence-based design

findings.antecedent: Buildings with windows / punched windows / symmetrical areas of high contrast
findings.consequent: Viewers focus on facade, spend more time looking, more likely to make a memory of the place, increased visual engagement, caught the eye

findings.antecedent: Blank facades / enormous glass facades
findings.consequent: Viewers ignore, get little attention, less visual engagement, brain informs nothing of import lies ahead, implicitly 'avoidant'

findings.antecedent: Human form / faces in images (e.g., man on raft, people crossing street, faces on banners)
findings.consequent: Brain is hardwired to look for and focus on, grabs attention, creates reddest heat map, people matter more

findings.antecedent: Presence of orientation points (e.g., water tower on High Bridge)
findings.consequent: People instinctively use for orientation, focus on distant objects

findings.antecedent: Absence of orientation points (e.g., water tower removed from High Bridge image)
findings.consequent: Brain does not let viewers focus on other side, attention directed to close-in surroundings (railings, walkway), attention dispersed, movement hampered, less likely to cross bridge

findings.antecedent: Car-centric subdivisions (e.g., Ayer, MA)
findings.consequent: Viewers implicitly look straight ahead and skyward (at trees), gaze path moves skyward, harder for pedestrians to move, brain focuses skyward, people don't walk

findings.antecedent: New urbanist housing / old-fashioned housing with building edges (e.g., Devens, MA)
findings.consequent: Gaze path follows building edges, viewers stay focused at grade level, invites people to walk, houses with porches/columns grab attention

findings.antecedent: Modern architecture (post-WWI, unface-like, blank, minimal detail, rectilinear)
findings.consequent: Harder for normal population to look at, implicitly feel less safe/secure, leads to anomie and disconnection, avoidant, stressful for nervous system, placelessness, inhumane habitats

findings.antecedent: Founding fathers of Modern Architecture with mental disorders (PTSD, ASD)
findings.consequent: Design outcomes reflect internal brain damage/atypical perception, unface-like and blank architecture, difficulty processing visual stimuli normally, inability to understand what people need to feel soothed/safe

findings.antecedent: Traumatic experience (e.g., WWI)
findings.consequent: Alters internal brain structure, rewires the brain, changes human perception of risk/safety, leads to dissociation, face-aversion, diminished visual complexity preference, 'blurry vision'

findings.antecedent: Human brain size (relative to body mass)
findings.consequent: Outlier in animal kingdom, enables complex thinking, requires high energy consumption (20-25% of body's energy intake)

findings.antecedent: Cooked diet (vs. raw diet)
findings.consequent: Promoted near doubling of brain neurons in ancestors, crucial step in human brain evolution
